key_insight: A physics-guided neural differential equation reduced-order model can capture nonlinear, multi-mode aeroelastic buffet dynamics by combining oscillator physics, Volterra memory effects, and a neural correction.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables fast prediction of aeroelastic stability, lock-in, and limit-cycle amplitudes from a single CFD training case, reducing reliance on expensive full-order simulations.
method: Nonlinear fluid oscillator + finite-memory multi-input Volterra series
Neural network correction for residual dynamics
Generalized to multiple structural modes and coupled to structural equations of motion
evidence_signal: The model is identified from one prescribed-motion CFD simulation and validated on transonic buffet over the ONERA OAT15A airfoil, where it matches reference aeroelastic stability, frequency lock-in, and limit-cycle amplitudes.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the single training maneuver excites all retained modes and may be sensitive when extrapolating beyond the tested flow and structural conditions.
paper_title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for Oscillatory Flows in Aeroelasticity with Application to Transonic Buffet
